scenario: A commodity dashboard records coffee-futures contract sizes only when they exceed 500 tons. A market analyst wants the average contract size across all trades.

data.description: Only contracts above 500 tons are observed. Contract size is Normal with known sigma 120 tons.

question: Estimate (a) the true mean contract size mu across all trades and (b) the fraction of trades recorded in the dashboard.
naive_answer: Average contract size is about 563 tons because that is the dashboard mean.
naive_trap: The dashboard truncates away smaller contracts.
reasoning_trace: Solve 563.02 = mu + 120*lambda((500-mu)/120). The solution is mu≈380 and recorded fraction sf(1.0)=0.1587.
python_verification:
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
def eq(mu): a=(500-mu)/120; return mu+120*norm.pdf(a)/norm.sf(a)-563.02
mu=brentq(eq,-500,499.99)
frac=norm.sf((500-mu)/120)
assert abs(mu-380)<6 and abs(frac-0.1587)<0.005
